chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Hakam from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Regarding shortening the prayer, he said, 'A bariq in a bariq is twenty-four miles.' Then he said, 'Indeed, my father used to say, 'Shortening is not prescribed for the white mule or the sound beast, but it is prescribed for the pace of the caravan.''
ai.seo_question: What is the defined distance for shortening prayers in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific distance for shortening prayers (qasr) as twenty-four miles, a measurement derived from the standard pace of a caravan (sair al-qitar) rather than slower mounts like a mule. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical travel conditions, ensuring the ruling reflects the actual duration and effort of typical journeying rather than theoretical maximums.
